readings.title: Shelomoh's Benediction
readings.subtitle: A Blessing Upon the Assembly of Yisra’ěl
readings.text: [1 Kings 8:54] And it came to be, when Shelomoh had ended praying <dn>את</dn> all this prayer and supplication to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that he rose up from before the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to the heavens. [55] And he stood and blessed all the assembly of Yisra’ěl with a loud voice, saying, [56] “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who has given rest to <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl, according to all that <dn>He</dn> promised. There has not failed one word of all <dn>His</dn> good word, which <dn>He</dn> promised through <dn>His</dn> servant Mosheh. [57] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is with us as <dn>He</dn> was with our fathers – <dn>He</dn> does not leave us nor forsake us – [58] to incline our hearts to <dn>Himself</dn>, to walk in all <dn>His</dn> ways, and to guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> laws and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings, which <dn>He</dn> commanded our fathers. [59] “And let these words of mine, with which <dn>I</dn> have made supplication before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, be near <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> day and night, to maintain <dn>את</dn> the cause of <dn>His</dn> servant and <dn>את</dn> the cause of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl, the matter of each day in its day, [60] so that all the peoples of the earth might know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>, there is no one else. [61] “Let your heart therefore be perfect to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to walk in <dn>His</dn> laws and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands, as at this day.”

readings.title: Dedication Sacrifices and Feast
readings.subtitle: The Fourteen-Day Celebration Concludes
readings.text: [1 Kings 8:62] And the sovereign and all Yisra’ěl with him slaughtered slaughterings before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [63] And Shelomoh slaughtered <dn>את</dn> the slaughtering of peace offerings, which he slaughtered to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, twenty-two thousand bulls and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. Thus the sovereign and all the children of Yisra’ěl dedicated <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [64] On that day the sovereign set apart <dn>את</dn> the middle of the courtyard that was in front of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for there he made <dn>את</dn> the ascending offerings, and <dn>את</dn> the grain offerings, and <dn>את</dn> the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze slaughter-place that was before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was too small to contain <dn>את</dn> the ascending offerings, and <dn>את</dn> the grain offerings, and <dn>את</dn> the fat of the peace offerings. [65] And Shelomoh at that time performed <dn>את</dn> the Festival, and all Yisra’ěl with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Ḥamath to the wadi of Mitsrayim, before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, seven days and seven days – fourteen days. [66] On the eighth day he sent <dn>את</dn> the people away. And they blessed <dn>את</dn> the sovereign, and went to their tents rejoicing and glad of heart for all the goodness that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had done for <dn>His</dn> servant Daviḏ, and for Yisra’ěl <dn>His</dn> people.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Glory Fills the Temple
readings.subtitle: Fire from Heaven Consumes the Offerings
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 7:1] And when Shelomoh had finished praying, fire came down from the heavens and consumed <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering and <dn>את</dn> the slaughterings. And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> filled <dn>את</dn> the House. [2] And the priests were unable to enter the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had filled <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] And all the children of Yisra’ěl saw <dn>את</dn> the fire coming down, and the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the House, and they bowed their faces to the ground on the pavement, and did obeisance and gave thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “For <dn>He</dn> is good, for <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment is everlasting.” [4] And the sovereign and all the people slaughtered a slaughtering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [5] And Sovereign Shelomoh slaughtered <dn>את</dn> a slaughtering of twenty-two thousand bulls and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. Thus the sovereign and all the people dedicated <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [6] And the priests, appointed to their duties, were standing, and the Lěvites with instruments of song of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which Sovereign Daviḏ had made to give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – for <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment is everlasting – whenever Daviḏ praised by their hand. And the priests sounded trumpets opposite them, while all Yisra’ěl was standing. [7] And Shelomoh set apart <dn>את</dn> the middle of the courtyard that was in front of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For there he made <dn>את</dn> the ascending offerings and <dn>את</dn> the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze slaughter-place which Shelomoh had made was not able to hold <dn>את</dn> the ascending offerings and <dn>את</dn> the grain offerings and <dn>את</dn> the fat. [8] And at that time Shelomoh performed <dn>את</dn> the festival seven days, and all Yisra’ěl with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Ḥamath to the wadi of Mitsrayim. [9] And on the eighth day they held a closing festival, for they performed the dedication of the slaughter-place seven days, and the festival seven days. [10] And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent <dn>את</dn> the people away to their tents, rejoicing and glad of heart for the goodness that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had done for Daviḏ, and for Shelomoh, and for Yisra’ěl <dn>His</dn> people.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Covenant with Shelomoh
readings.subtitle: A Conditional Promise of Blessing or Curse
readings.text: [1 Kings 9:1] And it came to be, when Shelomoh had finished building <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign, and <dn>את</dn> all the desire of Shelomoh which he was pleased to do, [2] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Shelomoh the second time, as <dn>He</dn> had appeared to him at Gib‛on. [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> your prayer and <dn>את</dn> your supplication that you have made before <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> have set <dn>את</dn> this house apart which you have built to put <dn>My</dn> Name there forever, and <dn>My</dn> eyes and <dn>My</dn> heart shall always be there.</dq> [4] <dq>“And you, if you walk before <dn>Me</dn> as your father Daviḏ walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that <dn>I</dn> have commanded you, if you guard <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> right-rulings,</dq> [5] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of your reign over Yisra’ěl forever, as <dn>I</dn> promised Daviḏ your father, saying, ‘There is not to cease a man of yours on the throne of Yisra’ěl.’</dq> [6] <dq>“If you at all turn back, you or your sons, from following <dn>Me</dn>, and do not guard <dn>My</dn> commands, <dn>My</dn> laws, which <dn>I</dn> have set before you, but shall go and serve other mighty ones and bow yourselves to them,</dq> [7] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from the face of the soil which <dn>I</dn> have given them, and <dn>את</dn> this house which <dn>I</dn> have set apart for <dn>My</dn> Name <dn>I</dn> shall send away from <dn>My</dn> presence. And Yisra’ěl shall be a proverb and a mockery among all the peoples.</dq> [8] <dq>“And this house, which has been exalted, everyone who passes by it shall be astonished, and hiss, and say, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> done thus to this land and to this house?’</dq> [9] <dq>“Then they shall say, ‘Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought <dn>את</dn> their fathers out of the land of Mitsrayim, and they took hold of other mighty ones, and bowed themselves to them and served them. That is why <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought <dn>את</dn> all this evil on them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Second Appearance to Shelomoh
readings.subtitle: The Conditions of the Covenant Reaffirmed
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 7:11] Thus Shelomoh finished <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign. And Shelomoh prosperously did <dn>את</dn> all that came into his heart to do in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and in his own house. [12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Shelomoh by night, and said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> your prayer, and have chosen this place for <dn>Myself</dn> as a house of slaughtering.</dq> [13] <dq>“If <dn>I</dn> shut up the heavens and there is no rain, or if <dn>I</dn> command the locusts to devour <dn>את</dn> the land, or if <dn>I</dn> send pestilence among <dn>My</dn> people,</dq> [14] <dq>and <dn>My</dn> people on whom <dn>My</dn> Name is called, shall humble themselves, and pray and seek <dn>My</dn> face, and turn from their evil ways, then <dn>I</dn> shall hear from the heavens, and forgive their sin and heal <dn>את</dn> their land.</dq> [15] <dq>“Now, <dn>My</dn> eyes are open and <dn>My</dn> ears attentive to the prayer of this place.</dq> [16] <dq>“And now, <dn>I</dn> have chosen and set apart <dn>את</dn> this house for <dn>My</dn> Name to be there forever. And <dn>My</dn> eyes and <dn>My</dn> heart shall be there all the days.</dq> [17] <dq>“And you, if you walk before <dn>Me</dn> as your father Daviḏ walked, and do according to all that <dn>I</dn> have commanded you, and if you guard <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> right-rulings,</dq> [18] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of your reign, as <dn>I</dn> covenanted with Daviḏ your father, saying, ‘There is not to cease a man of yours to rule Yisra’ěl.’</dq> [19] <dq>“But if you turn away and forsake <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> commands which <dn>I</dn> have set before you, and go and serve other mighty ones, and bow down to them,</dq> [20] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall pluck them from <dn>My</dn> land which <dn>I</dn> have given them, and this house which <dn>I</dn> have set apart for <dn>My</dn> Name <dn>I</dn> shall cast out of <dn>My</dn> sight. And <dn>I</dn> shall make it a proverb and a mockery among all peoples.</dq> [21] <dq>“And this house, which has been exalted, everyone who passes by it shall be astonished, and say, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> done thus to this land and to this house?’</dq> [22] <dq>“And they shall say, ‘Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, and have taken hold of other mighty ones, and bowed down to them and served them. That is why <dn>He</dn> has brought <dn>את</dn> all this evil on them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Shelomoh's Transaction with Hiram
readings.subtitle: Twenty Cities in Galil Exchanged for Temple Materials
readings.text: [1 Kings 9:10] And it came to be, at the end of twenty years, that Shelomoh had built <dn>את</dn> the two houses, <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign. [11] Ḥiram the sovereign of Tsor had supplied <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh with cedar and cypress and gold, as much as he desired. Then Sovereign Shelomoh gave Ḥiram twenty cities in the land of Galil. [12] And Ḥiram came from Tsor to see <dn>את</dn> the cities which Shelomoh had given him, but they were not right in his eyes, [13] and he said, “What are these cities you have given me, my brother?” And he called them the land of Kaḇul, as they are to this day. [14] And Ḥiram sent the sovereign one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
